newsitem.title: USA: CBOT's Arbor responds to report of CFTC inquiry.
newsitem.headline: CBOT's Arbor responds to report of CFTC inquiry.

text.p: Chicago Board of Trade chairman Patrick Arbor responded to a media report that the Commodity Futures Trading Commission was looking into his personal trading during the volatile expiration of the March wheat futures contract at the CBOT last year.
Arbor said he had cooperated with the CFTC in a routine inquiry regarding the wheat expiration.
"I have supplied them with all relevant records which show that my trading practices were beyond reproach," Arbor said in a statement released by the exchange.
"For the record, I did no trades on March wheat nor did I hold a position on March wheat," Arbor said in the statement.
Arbor went on to express outrage at the regulator for allowing the inquiry to become public.
"I am appalled that the CFTC has allowed a routine inquiry to end up in the media. It's a gross violation of my privacy and exhibits a lack of professionalism on the part of the CFTC," Arbor said.
A Dow Jones report today quoted a draft letter from the CFTC Enforcement Division concerning questions about Arbor's actions last spring during the expiration of March 1996 wheat futures.

The report said the CFTC wanted to know more about three orders in the July 1996 wheat futures contract that Arbor placed for his own account just after the close of trading in the expiring March contract.
On March 20 last year the March wheat contract jumped more than $2.00 per bushel minutes before the contract expired, peaking at a record high of $7.50.

Late last year CFTC staff said the CBOT's disciplinary actions, including letters of reprimand to traders involved in the runup in wheat prices during the March contract expiry, were "inadequate...and may not sufficiently deter future conduct."
The CFTC staff also pointed out that firms involved in the trading were treated differently than individual exchange members.
Arbor said in his statement that he would "continue to offer my full and total cooperation to satisfy their concerns."
